area_overview: Invalid/ambiguous local times caused by DST transitions and how to choose business policies for scheduling, display, audit, and automation.
key_ideas: Some local wall-clock times do not exist in a timezone because the clock jumps forward.
Some local wall-clock times occur twice because the clock falls back.
TimeZoneInfo.IsInvalidTime can detect nonexistent local times.
TimeZoneInfo.IsAmbiguousTime and GetAmbiguousTimeOffsets can detect and inspect repeated local times.
There is no universal correct rule for invalid/ambiguous times; the system must choose a business policy.
Common invalid-time policies are: move forward to the next valid local time, skip the occurrence, move backward, or reject as invalid.
Common ambiguous-time policies are: choose earlier occurrence, choose later occurrence, run only once by a fixed rule, or run twice.
Use clear names in code and APIs: earlier/later occurrence, invalid local time, ambiguous local time, offset choice.
Use TimeSpan for scheduling delays/timeouts after a concrete instant has been chosen.
